सीमांत अभिकर्मक वह अभिकारक होता है जो अभिक्रिया में सर्वप्रथम पूर्णतः समाप्त होता है। इसका निर्धारण अभिकारकों के मोलों को संतुलित समीकरण के स्टॉइकियोमीट्री गुणांकों से भाग देकर किया जाता है। कम द्रव्यमान वाला अभिकारक भी आधिक्य में हो सकता है यदि उसका मोलर द्रव्यमान कम हो (उदाहरणार्थ, \(2.0\text{ g}\) \(\text{H}_2\) और \(16.0\text{ g}\) \(\text{O}_2\) में \(\text{O}_2\) सीमांत अभिकर्मक है)। अतः न्यूनतम द्रव्यमान वाले अभिकारक के सीमांत होने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 2: द्वितीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
मूलानुपाती सूत्र किसी यौगिक में उपस्थित विभिन्न तत्वों के परमाणुओं के सरलतम पूर्णांक अनुपात को दर्शाता है, जबकि एक अणु में उपस्थित परमाणुओं की वास्तविक संख्या को आण्विक सूत्र प्रदर्शित करता है (जैसे हाइड्रोजन परॉक्साइड का मूलानुपाती सूत्र \(\text{HO}\) तथा आण्विक सूत्र \(\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\) है)। अतः मूलानुपाती सूत्र द्वारा वास्तविक संख्या दर्शाने का विवरण गलत है।

चरण 3: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
दोनों कथन गलत हैं क्योंकि सीमांत अभिकर्मक प्रारंभिक द्रव्यमान के बजाय मोलर स्टॉइकियोमीट्री पर निर्भर करता है, और मूलानुपाती सूत्र वास्तविक परमाणुओं की संख्या के बजाय सरलतम पूर्णांक अनुपात को दर्शाता है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q01 - Characteristics and classification of matter

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Particles in a solid are closely packed in an orderly arrangement with restricted mobility, giving solids a definite shape and volume.

Statement II: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout, and its constituent components cannot be seen separately.

Statement III: Constituents of a chemical compound can be separated into their constituent elements by simple physical filtration or distillation.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: ठोस में कण एक सुव्यवस्थित क्रम में बहुत पास-पास होते हैं और उनकी गतिशीलता सीमित होती है, जिससे ठोसों का एक निश्चित आकार और आयतन होता है।

कथन II: एक समांगी मिश्रण का संघटन सर्वत्र एकसमान होता है, और इसके घटक भागों को अलग-अलग नहीं देखा जा सकता है।

कथन III: किसी रासायनिक यौगिक के संघटकों को साधारण भौतिक निस्यंदन या आसवन द्वारा उनके संघटक तत्वों में पृथक किया जा सकता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Scientific Evaluation of the First Assertion
In the solid state, intermolecular forces hold the constituent particles closely in fixed positions, permitting only vibrational motion about their mean positions. As a result, solids maintain both a definite volume and a distinct shape. Therefore, the assertion regarding particle arrangement and definiteness of shape and volume in solids is correct.

Step 2: Scientific Evaluation of the Second Assertion
A homogeneous mixture is characterised by completely uniform distribution of its component particles throughout the bulk, such that no distinct phase boundaries exist (for example, a completely dissolved sugar solution or clean air). Thus, the assertion regarding uniform composition and indistinguishable components in homogeneous mixtures is correct.

Step 3: Scientific Evaluation of the Third Assertion
A compound consists of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed stoichiometric proportions. The constituent atoms are joined by chemical bonds, which cannot be cleaved by physical separation techniques like filtration or distillation; only chemical or electrochemical methods can decompose a compound. Hence, the claim that compounds can be separated physically is incorrect.

Step 4: Conceptual Conclusion
Only the first and second assertions are correct, while the third assertion regarding physical separation of compounds is incorrect.

चरण 1: प्रथम विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
ठोस अवस्था में, अंतरा-अणुक बल संघटक कणों को उनके निश्चित स्थानों पर दृढ़ता से बांधे रखते हैं, जिससे वे केवल अपनी माध्य स्थितियों के परितः दोलन कर सकते हैं। परिणामस्वरूप, ठोसों का एक निश्चित आयतन और निश्चित आकार होता है। अतः ठोसों में कणों की व्यवस्था और निश्चित आकार व आयतन से संबंधित विवरण सही है।

चरण 2: द्वितीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
समांगी मिश्रण की यह विशेषता होती है कि उसके घटक कण संपूर्ण निकाय में पूर्णतः एकसमान रूप से वितरित रहते हैं, जिससे कोई पृथक सीमाएं नहीं दिखाई देती हैं (जैसे जल में घुली शर्करा अथवा स्वच्छ वायु)। अतः समांगी मिश्रण के एकसमान संघटन से संबंधित विवरण सही है।

चरण 3: तृतीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
यौगिक में दो या दो से अधिक तत्व रासायनिक रूप से निश्चित अनुपात में जुड़े होते हैं। घटक परमाणु रासायनिक बंधों द्वारा बंधे होते हैं, जिन्हें निस्यंदन या आसवन जैसी भौतिक विधियों द्वारा तोड़ा नहीं जा सकता; यौगिकों को केवल रासायनिक या विद्युत-रासायनिक विधियों द्वारा ही अपघटित किया जा सकता है। अतः यौगिकों के भौतिक पृथक्करण का दावा गलत है।

चरण 4: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
केवल प्रथम और द्वितीय विवरण सही हैं, जबकि यौगिकों के भौतिक पृथक्करण से संबंधित तृतीय विवरण गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q02 - Laws of chemical combination and Dalton atomic theory

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Antoine Lavoisier established that in all physical and chemical changes, the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants.

Statement II: The law of multiple proportions states that when two elements form more than one compound, the masses of one element combining with a fixed mass of the other element bear a simple whole-number ratio.

Statement III: Joseph Proust demonstrated that a synthetic sample of cupric carbonate contains a significantly higher percentage of copper than a naturally occurring sample.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: आंत्वान लावोईसिए ने स्थापित किया कि सभी भौतिक और रासायनिक परिवर्तनों में, उत्पादों का कुल द्रव्यमान अभिकारकों के कुल द्रव्यमान के बराबर होता है।

कथन II: गुणित अनुपात का नियम यह बताता है कि जब दो तत्व एक से अधिक यौगिक बनाते हैं, तो एक तत्व के विभिन्न द्रव्यमान जो दूसरे तत्व के एक निश्चित द्रव्यमान से संयोग करते हैं, एक सरल पूर्णांक अनुपात में होते हैं।

कथन III: जोसेफ प्राउस्ट ने प्रदर्शित किया कि क्यूप्रिक कार्बोनेट के संश्लेषित नमूने में प्राकृतिक रूप से पाए जाने वाले नमूने की तुलना में कॉपर का प्रतिशत काफी अधिक होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Scientific Evaluation of the First Assertion
The law of conservation of mass, formulated by Antoine Lavoisier in 1789 through quantitative combustion experiments, states that matter is neither created nor destroyed during chemical transformations. Hence, the total mass of the products always equals the total mass of the reactants. Therefore, this assertion is correct.

Step 2: Scientific Evaluation of the Second Assertion
The law of multiple proportions, proposed by John Dalton in 1803, states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound (such as \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) and \(\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\)), the different masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element bear a ratio of small whole numbers (e.g., \(16\text{ g} : 32\text{ g} = 1 : 2\)). Thus, this assertion is correct.

Step 3: Scientific Evaluation of the Third Assertion
Joseph Proust established the law of definite proportions by analyzing both natural and synthetic samples of cupric carbonate (\(\text{CuCO}_3\)) and found identical percentages by mass for each element: \(51.35\%\) copper, \(9.74\%\) carbon, and \(38.91\%\) oxygen. He did not observe a higher copper percentage in the synthetic sample. Hence, the assertion claiming differing percentages is incorrect.

Step 4: Conceptual Conclusion
Only the first and second assertions are correct, while the assertion regarding differing copper percentages in cupric carbonate samples is incorrect.

चरण 1: प्रथम विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
द्रव्यमान संरक्षण का नियम, जिसे आंत्वान लावोईसिए ने 1789 में दहन अभिक्रियाओं के सटीक प्रयोगों द्वारा प्रतिपादित किया था, यह बताता है कि रासायनिक परिवर्तनों में द्रव्यमान न तो बनता है और न ही नष्ट होता है। अतः उत्पादों का कुल द्रव्यमान सदैव अभिकारकों के कुल द्रव्यमान के बराबर होता है। इसलिए यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 2: द्वितीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
गुणित अनुपात का नियम, जिसे 1803 में जॉन डाल्टन ने प्रतिपादित किया था, यह बताता है कि जब दो तत्व एक से अधिक यौगिक बनाते हैं (जैसे \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) और \(\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\)), तो एक तत्व के वे द्रव्यमान जो दूसरे तत्व के एक निश्चित द्रव्यमान से संयोग करते हैं, परस्पर सरल पूर्णांक अनुपात (जैसे \(16\text{ g} : 32\text{ g} = 1 : 2\)) में होते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 3: तृतीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
जोसेफ प्राउस्ट ने क्यूप्रिक कार्बोनेट (\(\text{CuCO}_3\)) के प्राकृतिक और संश्लेषित दोनों नमूनों का विश्लेषण करके स्थिर अनुपात का नियम सिद्ध किया था, जिसमें दोनों में तत्वों का प्रतिशत समान पाया गया था: \(51.35\%\) कॉपर, \(9.74\%\) कार्बन, और \(38.91\%\) ऑक्सीजन। उन्होंने संश्लेषित नमूने में अधिक कॉपर नहीं पाया था। अतः भिन्न प्रतिशत का दावा गलत है।

चरण 4: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
केवल प्रथम और द्वितीय विवरण सही हैं, जबकि क्यूप्रिक कार्बोनेट के नमूनों में भिन्न कॉपर प्रतिशत से संबंधित विवरण गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q03 - Uncertainty in measurement precision accuracy and significant figures

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Precision refers to the closeness of several repeated measurements for the same physical quantity to one another.

Statement II: Zeros preceding the first non-zero digit in a decimal number are non-significant and only indicate the position of the decimal point.

Statement III: Counting numbers of discrete objects, such as 20 eggs or 2 balls, possess only one significant figure because they are integers.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: परिशुद्धता एक ही भौतिक राशि के लिए लिए गए कई दोहराए गए मापों के एक-दूसरे के सन्निकट होने को संदर्भित करती है।

कथन II: किसी दशमलव संख्या में प्रथम अशून्य अंक से पहले आने वाले शून्य सार्थक नहीं होते हैं और वे केवल दशमलव बिंदु की स्थिति को दर्शाते हैं।

कथन III: पृथक वस्तुओं की गिनती की संख्या, जैसे 20 अंडे या 2 गेंदें, में केवल एक ही सार्थक अंक होता है क्योंकि वे पूर्णांक हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Scientific Evaluation of the First Assertion
Precision expresses the agreement or reproducibility among multiple experimental determinations of the same quantity under identical conditions. In contrast, accuracy expresses agreement between a measured value and the true accepted value. Therefore, defining precision as the closeness of repeated measurements to each other is correct.

Step 2: Scientific Evaluation of the Second Assertion
According to the fundamental rules of significant figures, leading zeros located before the first non-zero digit (such as in \(0.0052\)) serve solely as place-holders to establish the decimal point and do not contribute to precision. Thus, such zeros are non-significant, making this assertion correct.

Step 3: Scientific Evaluation of the Third Assertion
Exact numbers obtained by counting discrete objects (for instance, \(2\) balls or \(20\) eggs) have an infinite number of significant figures because they can be represented with an unlimited succession of trailing zeros after a decimal point (\(2.000000...\) or \(20.000000...\)). Therefore, the claim that counting numbers have only one significant figure is incorrect.

Step 4: Conceptual Conclusion
Only the first and second assertions are correct, whereas attributing a single significant figure to exact counting numbers is incorrect.

चरण 1: प्रथम विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
परिशुद्धता समान परिस्थितियों में एक ही राशि के लिए किए गए कई मापों के परस्पर निकट होने अथवा पुनरुत्पादकता को दर्शाती है। इसके विपरीत, यथार्थता मापे गए मान और वास्तविक मान के बीच की सहमति को दर्शाती है। अतः परिशुद्धता को मापों की परस्पर निकटता के रूप में परिभाषित करना सही है।

चरण 2: द्वितीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
सार्थक अंकों के नियमों के अनुसार, प्रथम अशून्य अंक से पहले आने वाले शून्य (जैसे \(0.0052\) में) केवल दशमलव बिंदु की स्थिति को इंगित करते हैं और वे सार्थक नहीं होते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 3: तृतीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
पृथक वस्तुओं की गिनती से प्राप्त निश्चित संख्याओं (जैसे \(2\) गेंदें अथवा \(20\) अंडे) में सार्थक अंकों की संख्या अनंत होती है, क्योंकि इन्हें दशमलव के बाद अनंत शून्य लगाकर व्यक्त किया जा सकता है (\(2.000000...\) अथवा \(20.000000...\))। अतः गिनती की संख्याओं में केवल एक सार्थक अंक होने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 4: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
केवल प्रथम और द्वितीय विवरण सही हैं, जबकि निश्चित गिनती संख्याओं में केवल एक सार्थक अंक होने का विवरण गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q04 - Temperature dependence of concentration terms and limiting reagent

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Molality and mole fraction do not change with temperature variations because both are defined strictly with respect to mass.

Statement II: The molarity of an aqueous solution decreases as the temperature increases due to thermal expansion of the solution volume.

Statement III: The limiting reagent in a chemical reaction is the reactant whose initial mole count divided by its stoichiometric coefficient is the smallest.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: मोललता और मोल अंश ताप में परिवर्तनों के साथ नहीं बदलते हैं क्योंकि दोनों को पूर्णतः द्रव्यमान के संदर्भ में परिभाषित किया जाता है।

कथन II: ताप बढ़ने पर विलयन के आयतन के तापीय प्रसार के कारण जलीय विलयन की मोलरता घट जाती है।

कथन III: रासायनिक अभिक्रिया में सीमांत अभिकर्मक वह अभिकारक होता है जिसके प्रारंभिक मोलों की संख्या को उसके स्टॉइकियोमीट्री गुणांक से विभाजित करने पर न्यूनतम मान प्राप्त होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Scientific Evaluation of the First Assertion
Molality is defined as moles of solute per kilogram of solvent (\(m = n_{\text{solute}} / w_{\text{solvent}}\)), and mole fraction is the ratio of moles of a component to total moles in the mixture. Because mass and amount of substance (moles) are intrinsic quantities that do not expand or contract with temperature, both molality and mole fraction are strictly independent of temperature. Therefore, this assertion is correct.

Step 2: Scientific Evaluation of the Second Assertion
Molarity is defined as moles of solute per litre of solution (\(M = n / V\)). When an aqueous solution is heated, it undergoes volumetric thermal expansion, thereby increasing the total solution volume \(V\). Since volume appears in the denominator, the molarity of the solution decreases with increasing temperature. Thus, this assertion is correct.

Step 3: Scientific Evaluation of the Third Assertion
To determine the limiting reagent in a reaction, the moles of each reactant initially provided are divided by their respective stoichiometric coefficients from the balanced chemical equation. The reactant exhibiting the smallest ratio \(n / \nu\) will be exhausted first, thereby terminating further product formation. Hence, this quantitative criterion for the limiting reagent is correct.

Step 4: Conceptual Conclusion
All three assertions are scientifically correct as temperature independence of mass preserves molality, volumetric expansion reduces molarity, and the smallest stoichiometric mole ratio identifies the limiting reagent.

चरण 1: प्रथम विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
मोललता को प्रति किलोग्राम विलायक में विलेय के मोलों (\(m = n_{\text{विलेय}} / w_{\text{विलायक}}\)) और मोल अंश को कुल मोलों के सापेक्ष किसी घटक के मोल अनुपात के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है। चूंकि द्रव्यमान और पदार्थ की मात्रा (मोल) ताप के साथ परिवर्तित नहीं होते हैं, अतः मोललता और मोल अंश दोनों ताप पर निर्भर नहीं करते हैं। इसलिए यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 2: द्वितीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
मोलरता को प्रति लीटर विलयन में विलेय के मोलों (\(M = n / V\)) के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है। जलीय विलयन को गर्म करने पर उसका तापीय प्रसार होता है, जिससे कुल आयतन \(V\) बढ़ जाता है। चूंकि आयतन हर में आता है, अतः ताप बढ़ने पर मोलरता घट जाती है। इसलिए यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 3: तृतीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
अभिक्रिया में सीमांत अभिकर्मक ज्ञात करने के लिए, प्रत्येक अभिकारक के दिए गए मोलों को संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण में उनके संबंधित स्टॉइकियोमीट्री गुणांकों से विभाजित किया जाता है। जिस अभिकारक का यह अनुपात \(n / \nu\) न्यूनतम होता है, वह पहले समाप्त होकर अभिक्रिया को सीमित कर देता है। अतः सीमांत अभिकर्मक का यह मानदंड सही है।

चरण 4: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
तीनों विवरण वैज्ञानिक रूप से सही हैं क्योंकि द्रव्यमान की ताप-स्वतंत्रता मोललता को स्थिर रखती है, आयतन प्रसार मोलरता को घटाता है, और न्यूनतम स्टॉइकियोमीट्री अनुपात सीमांत अभिकर्मक की पहचान करता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q01 - Fundamental laws of chemical combination and atomic mass standard

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: The law of definite proportions remains valid irrespective of whether a given compound is isolated from natural sources or synthesised in a laboratory.

Statement II: According to Gay-Lussac's law, gases combine or are produced in a chemical reaction in a simple whole-number ratio by volume, provided all gases are measured at the same temperature and pressure.

Statement III: One unified atomic mass unit (\(\text{u}\)) is presently defined as a mass exactly equal to one-sixteenth of the mass of an isolated oxygen-16 atom.

Statement IV: Dalton's atomic theory successfully provided an atomic explanation for the laws of chemical combination by mass, but failed to explain Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.

Which of the above statements are correct?

निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: स्थिर अनुपात का नियम इस बात पर निर्भर किए बिना मान्य रहता है कि कोई यौगिक प्राकृतिक स्रोतों से प्राप्त किया गया है अथवा प्रयोगशाला में संश्लेषित किया गया है।

कथन II: गे-लुसाक के नियमानुसार, रासायनिक अभिक्रिया में गैसें आयतन के एक सरल पूर्णांक अनुपात में संयोग करती हैं अथवा उत्पन्न होती हैं, बशर्ते सभी गैसें समान ताप और दाब पर मापी गई हों।

कथन III: एक एकीकृत परमाणु द्रव्यमान मात्रक (\(\text{u}\)) को वर्तमान में एक विलगित ऑक्सीजन-16 परमाणु के द्रव्यमान के ठीक 1/16वें भाग के बराबर परिभाषित किया गया है।

कथन IV: डाल्टन का परमाणु सिद्धांत द्रव्यमान पर आधारित रासायनिक संयोजन के नियमों की सफल परमाण्विक व्याख्या करने में समर्थ रहा, किंतु यह गे-लुसाक के गैसीय आयतन के नियम की व्याख्या करने में असमर्थ रहा।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Scientific Evaluation of the First Assertion
Joseph Proust established the law of definite proportions by confirming that natural and synthetic samples of cupric carbonate exhibit precisely identical weight percentages of copper, carbon, and oxygen. Hence, the proposition asserting the source-independent validity of the law of definite proportions is scientifically correct.

Step 2: Scientific Evaluation of the Second Assertion
Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes (1808) demonstrates that reacting and produced gases bear simple whole-number volumetric ratios when compared at identical temperature and pressure (such as 100 mL of hydrogen combining with 50 mL of oxygen to yield 100 mL of water vapour, a 2:1 ratio). Thus, the proposition defining Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes is correct.

Step 3: Scientific Evaluation of the Third Assertion
Under the international atomic mass scale established in 1961, one unified atomic mass unit (\(\text{u}\) or \(\text{amu}\)) is defined as exactly one-twelfth (\(1/12\)) of the mass of one carbon-12 (\(^{12}\text{C}\)) atom, not one-sixteenth of an oxygen-16 atom. Therefore, the definition based on oxygen-16 is factually and historically incorrect.

Step 4: Scientific Evaluation of the Fourth Assertion
John Dalton's atomic theory treated atoms as indivisible units, successfully explaining mass conservation and constant composition. However, because Dalton assumed that equal volumes of gases do not contain equal numbers of atoms/molecules and denied the existence of diatomic elementary molecules, his theory failed to explain Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes. Thus, this historical proposition is correct.

Step 5: Conceptual Conclusion
The first, second, and fourth propositions are scientifically and historically correct, whereas the third proposition defining the unified atomic mass unit via oxygen-16 is incorrect.

चरण 1: प्रथम विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
जोसेफ प्राउस्ट ने क्यूप्रिक कार्बोनेट के प्राकृतिक और संश्लेषित दोनों नमूनों में कॉपर, कार्बन और ऑक्सीजन के द्रव्यमान प्रतिशत को सर्वथा समान पाकर स्थिर अनुपात के नियम की पुष्टि की। अतः स्थिर अनुपात के नियम की स्रोत-निरपेक्षता से संबंधित विवरण वैज्ञानिक रूप से सही है।

चरण 2: द्वितीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
गे-लुसाक के गैसीय आयतन के नियम (1808) के अनुसार, समान ताप और दाब पर अभिक्रिया करने वाली तथा उत्पन्न होने वाली गैसों के आयतन सरल पूर्णांक अनुपात में होते हैं (जैसे 100 mL हाइड्रोजन 50 mL ऑक्सीजन से संयोग कर 100 mL जलवाष्प बनाती है, जो 2:1 अनुपात है)। अतः गैसीय आयतन के नियम का यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 3: तृतीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
1961 में स्वीकृत अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानक के अनुसार, एक एकीकृत परमाणु द्रव्यमान मात्रक (\(\text{u}\)) को कार्बन-12 (\(^{12}\text{C}\)) परमाणु के द्रव्यमान के ठीक 1/12वें भाग के बराबर परिभाषित किया गया है, ऑक्सीजन-16 के 1/16वें भाग के रूप में नहीं। अतः ऑक्सीजन-16 पर आधारित परिभाषा तथ्यात्मक रूप से गलत है।

चरण 4: चतुर्थ विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
जॉन डाल्टन के परमाणु सिद्धांत ने द्रव्यमान संरक्षण और स्थिर अनुपात के नियमों की व्याख्या सफलतापूर्वक की, किंतु गैसों की परमाणुकता और समान आयतनों में समान अणुओं की उपस्थिति को न स्वीकारने के कारण यह गे-लुसाक के गैसीय आयतन के नियम की व्याख्या नहीं कर सका। अतः डाल्टन के सिद्धांत की इस सीमा से संबंधित विवरण सही है।

चरण 5: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय और चतुर्थ विवरण वैज्ञानिक एवं ऐतिहासिक रूप से सही हैं, जबकि एकीकृत परमाणु द्रव्यमान मात्रक को ऑक्सीजन-16 द्वारा परिभाषित करने वाला तृतीय विवरण गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q02 - Mole concept empirical formula and solution concentration terms

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements:

Statement I: One mole of any chemical substance contains exactly \(6.02214076 \times 10^{23}\) elementary entities, representing the fixed numerical value of the Avogadro constant.

Statement II: The molecular formula of a compound is obtained by multiplying its empirical formula by an integer multiplier \(n\), where \(n = \frac{\text{Molar mass}}{\text{Empirical formula mass}}\).

Statement III: When \(50.0\text{ kg}\) of dinitrogen gas is reacted with \(10.0\text{ kg}\) of dihydrogen gas to synthesize ammonia, dinitrogen acts as the limiting reagent.

Statement IV: The molality of an aqueous solution remains invariant with temperature changes, whereas its molarity decreases as the temperature increases.

Which of the above statements are correct?

निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: किसी रासायनिक पदार्थ के एक मोल में ठीक \(6.02214076 \times 10^{23}\) मूल कण होते हैं, जो आवोगाद्रो नियतांक के निश्चित संख्यात्मक मान को दर्शाते हैं।

कथन II: किसी यौगिक का आण्विक सूत्र उसके मूलानुपाती सूत्र को एक पूर्णांक गुणक \(n\) से गुणा करके प्राप्त किया जाता है, जहाँ \(n = \frac{\text{मोलर द्रव्यमान}}{\text{मूलानुपाती सूत्र द्रव्यमान}}\) होता है।

कथन III: जब अमोनिया के संश्लेषण हेतु \(50.0\text{ kg}\) डाइनाइट्रोजन गैस की अभिक्रिया \(10.0\text{ kg}\) डाइहाइड्रोजन गैस से कराई जाती है, तो डाइनाइट्रोजन सीमांत अभिकर्मक के रूप में कार्य करती है।

कथन IV: किसी जलीय विलयन की मोललता ताप परिवर्तनों के साथ अपरिवर्तित रहती है, जबकि ताप बढ़ने पर उसकी मोलरता घट जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Scientific Evaluation of the First Assertion
Under the revised SI base unit definition, the mole is defined by setting the Avogadro constant \(N_A\) to the exact fixed numerical value of \(6.02214076 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}\). Thus, one mole of any substance contains exactly this number of specified elementary entities, making this assertion scientifically correct.

Step 2: Scientific Evaluation of the Second Assertion
The empirical formula expresses the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of different elements in a compound, while the molecular formula denotes the exact number of atoms in a molecule. The integral factor \(n\) relating the two formulas is evaluated directly by \(n = \frac{\text{Molar mass}}{\text{Empirical formula mass}}\). Therefore, this stoichiometric relationship is correct.

Step 3: Scientific Evaluation of the Third Assertion
In the balanced synthesis \(\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})\), \(50.0\text{ kg}\) of \(\text{N}_2\) corresponds to \(\frac{50000\text{ g}}{28.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 1.786 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\), which requires \(3 \times 1.786 \times 10^3 = 5.36 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\). However, only \(\frac{10000\text{ g}}{2.016\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 4.96 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\) is supplied. Because available \(\text{H}_2\) is less than stoichiometrically required, dihydrogen (\(\text{H}_2\)) is the limiting reagent, not dinitrogen (\(\text{N}_2\)). Thus, this claim is incorrect.

Step 4: Scientific Evaluation of the Fourth Assertion
Molality (\(m = n_{\text{solute}} / w_{\text{solvent}}\)) depends strictly on mass, which does not expand with temperature, keeping molality constant. Conversely, molarity (\(M = n / V\)) depends on volume; thermal volumetric expansion increases \(V\), thereby reducing molarity. Hence, this comparative statement on temperature dependence is correct.

Step 5: Conceptual Conclusion
The first, second, and fourth assertions are correct, whereas identifying dinitrogen as the limiting reagent is stoichiometrically incorrect.

चरण 1: प्रथम विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
संशोधित SI मात्रक प्रणाली के अनुसार, मोल को आवोगाद्रो नियतांक \(N_A\) के निश्चित संख्यात्मक मान \(6.02214076 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}\) द्वारा परिभाषित किया गया है। अतः किसी पदार्थ के 1 मोल में ठीक इतने ही मूल कण होते हैं, जिससे यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 2: द्वितीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
मूलानुपाती सूत्र परमाणुओं का सरलतम पूर्णांक अनुपात दर्शाता है जबकि आण्विक सूत्र वास्तविक परमाणुओं की संख्या दर्शाता है। दोनों के बीच पूर्णांक गुणक \(n = \frac{\text{मोलर द्रव्यमान}}{\text{मूलानुपाती सूत्र द्रव्यमान}}\) होता है। अतः यह सूत्र संबंध सही है।

चरण 3: तृतीय विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
संतुलित समीकरण \(\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})\) में, \(50.0\text{ kg}\) \(\text{N}_2\) (अर्थात \(1.786 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\)) को अभिक्रिया हेतु \(5.36 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\) \(\text{H}_2\) की आवश्यकता होती है। किंतु उपलब्ध \(\text{H}_2\) केवल \(4.96 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\) है। आवश्यक मात्रा से कम होने के कारण डाइहाइड्रोजन (\(\text{H}_2\)) सीमांत अभिकर्मक है, डाइनाइट्रोजन नहीं। अतः यह दावा गलत है।

चरण 4: चतुर्थ विवरण का वैज्ञानिक मूल्यांकन
मोललता द्रव्यमान पर निर्भर करती है जो ताप के साथ परिवर्तित नहीं होता, अतः मोललता स्थिर रहती है। दूसरी ओर, मोलरता आयतन पर निर्भर करती है; तापीय प्रसार से आयतन बढ़ने पर मोलरता घट जाती है। अतः ताप-निर्भरता से संबंधित यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 5: वैचारिक निष्कर्ष
प्रथम, द्वितीय और चतुर्थ विवरण सही हैं, जबकि डाइनाइट्रोजन को सीमांत अभिकर्मक बताने वाला तृतीय विवरण गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q01 - Ancient Indian chemistry texts and their contributions

questiontext.text:
Match the ancient Indian texts or treatises listed in List-I with their respective chemical or technological contributions described in List-II:

List-I (Treatise / Text)List-II (Contribution / Description)
(A) Rasaratnakara(p) Indigenous methods of preparing alkalis (kshar)
(B) Rasarnavam(q) Earliest Ayurvedic treatise on medicine mentioning reduction of particle size of metals
(C) Charaka Samhita(r) Work of Nagarjuna dealing with formulation of mercury compounds and extraction of metals
(D) Sushruta Samhita(s) Tantric text discussing the use of various furnaces, ovens, and crucibles

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the contribution of Rasaratnakara
Rasaratnakara is a seminal alchemical work authored by Nagarjuna that deals comprehensively with the formulation of mercury compounds and methods for the extraction and metallurgy of metals such as gold, silver, tin, and copper. Thus, Rasaratnakara pairs with the work of Nagarjuna dealing with formulation of mercury compounds and extraction of metals.

Step 2: Determine the contribution of Rasarnavam
Rasarnavam is a prominent Tantric text dating to approximately 800 CE that describes the construction and operational use of various furnaces, ovens, crucibles, and flame coloration tests. Thus, Rasarnavam pairs with the Tantric text discussing the use of various furnaces, ovens, and crucibles.

Step 3: Determine the contribution of Charaka Samhita
Charaka Samhita is the oldest surviving Ayurvedic treatise on internal medicine that details the preparation of bhasmas and the medicinal reduction of particle size of metals. Thus, Charaka Samhita pairs with the earliest Ayurvedic treatise on medicine mentioning reduction of particle size of metals.

Step 4: Determine the contribution of Sushruta Samhita
Sushruta Samhita is an ancient Ayurvedic surgical treatise that describes indigenous methods for the preparation and therapeutic application of alkalis (kshar). Thus, Sushruta Samhita pairs with the indigenous methods of preparing alkalis (kshar).

Step 5: Final conclusion
Combining these evaluations, the verified pairings are: Rasaratnakara corresponds to (r), Rasarnavam corresponds to (s), Charaka Samhita corresponds to (q), and Sushruta Samhita corresponds to (p). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(r), B-(s), C-(q), D-(p).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q02 - SI base physical quantities and their fundamental units

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities in List-I with their corresponding SI base units in List-II:

List-I (Physical Quantity)List-II (SI Base Unit)
(A) Amount of substance(p) Candela (\(\text{cd}\))
(B) Electric current(q) Mole (\(\text{mol}\))
(C) Luminous intensity(r) Kelvin (\(\text{K}\))
(D) Thermodynamic temperature(s) Ampere (\(\text{A}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the SI unit of amount of substance
The SI base unit for the amount of substance is the mole, abbreviated as \(\text{mol}\).

Step 2: Identify the SI unit of electric current
The SI base unit for electric current is the ampere, abbreviated as \(\text{A}\).

Step 3: Identify the SI unit of luminous intensity
The SI base unit for luminous intensity is the candela, abbreviated as \(\text{cd}\).

Step 4: Identify the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature
The SI base unit for thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin, abbreviated as \(\text{K}\).

Step 5: Final conclusion
Connecting each quantity to its canonical base unit gives: amount of substance corresponds to the mole (q), electric current corresponds to the ampere (s), luminous intensity corresponds to the candela (p), and thermodynamic temperature corresponds to the kelvin (r). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(q), B-(s), C-(p), D-(r).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q03 - SI prefixes and their decimal multiplication factors

questiontext.text:
Match the SI prefixes in List-I with their decimal multiplication factors in List-II:

List-I (Prefix)List-II (Multiplication Factor)
(A) Femto(p) \(10^{-12}\)
(B) Pico(q) \(10^{9}\)
(C) Micro(r) \(10^{-15}\)
(D) Giga(s) \(10^{-6}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the factor for femto
In the International System of Units, the prefix femto denotes a factor of \(10^{-15}\).

Step 2: Identify the factor for pico
The prefix pico denotes a submultiple factor of \(10^{-12}\).

Step 3: Identify the factor for micro
The prefix micro denotes a submultiple factor of \(10^{-6}\).

Step 4: Identify the factor for giga
The prefix giga denotes a multiple factor of \(10^{9}\).

Step 5: Final conclusion
Aligning each prefix with its decimal factor yields: femto corresponds to \(10^{-15}\) (r), pico corresponds to \(10^{-12}\) (p), micro corresponds to \(10^{-6}\) (s), and giga corresponds to \(10^{9}\) (q). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(r), B-(p), C-(s), D-(q).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q04 - Laws of chemical combination and proposing scientists

questiontext.text:
Match the laws of chemical combination in List-I with the scientists who proposed or formulated them in List-II:

List-I (Law of Chemical Combination)List-II (Formulated By)
(A) Law of Conservation of Mass(p) Joseph Proust (1799)
(B) Law of Definite Proportions(q) John Dalton (1803)
(C) Law of Multiple Proportions(r) Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac (1808)
(D) Law of Gaseous Volumes(s) Antoine Lavoisier (1789)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Associate Law of Conservation of Mass
The Law of Conservation of Mass states that matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. It was experimentally established by Antoine Lavoisier in 1789.

Step 2: Associate Law of Definite Proportions
The Law of Definite Proportions states that a given compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by weight. It was formulated by Joseph Proust in 1799.

Step 3: Associate Law of Multiple Proportions
The Law of Multiple Proportions states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in the ratio of small whole numbers. It was proposed by John Dalton in 1803.

Step 4: Associate Law of Gaseous Volumes
The Law of Gaseous Volumes states that when gases react together, they do so in volumes which bear a simple whole-number ratio to one another and to the volumes of the gaseous products, provided all measurements are made under identical conditions of temperature and pressure. It was discovered by Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac in 1808.

Step 5: Final conclusion
Matching each fundamental law with its originator gives: Law of Conservation of Mass corresponds to Antoine Lavoisier (s), Law of Definite Proportions corresponds to Joseph Proust (p), Law of Multiple Proportions corresponds to John Dalton (q), and Law of Gaseous Volumes corresponds to Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac (r). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(s), B-(p), C-(q), D-(r).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q05 - Classification of matter and illustrative chemical examples

questiontext.text:
Match the classifications of matter in List-I with their illustrative examples in List-II:

List-I (Classification of Matter)List-II (Illustrative Example)
(A) Homogeneous mixture(p) Completely dissolved aqueous glucose solution
(B) Heterogeneous mixture(q) Solid mixture of sodium chloride and grain particles
(C) Chemical element(r) Chemically pure copper wire
(D) Pure compound(s) Stoichiometric crystalline water ice

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify homogeneous mixture
A homogeneous mixture possesses a uniform composition and appearance throughout its bulk. An aqueous solution of glucose in water has its solute particles uniformly distributed at the molecular level, forming a single phase. Thus, it is a homogeneous mixture.

Step 2: Identify heterogeneous mixture
A heterogeneous mixture consists of two or more distinct phases with non-uniform composition. A mixture of solid grains and sodium chloride salt exhibits visible boundaries and variable local proportions. Thus, it is a heterogeneous mixture.

Step 3: Identify chemical element
An element consists of only one type of atom and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical reactions. Pure copper wire is composed entirely of copper atoms. Thus, it represents an element.

Step 4: Identify pure compound
A compound is composed of two or more different elements combined in a fixed ratio by mass with distinct chemical properties. Ice consists of water molecules with hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed \(1:8\) mass ratio. Thus, it represents a pure compound.

Step 5: Final conclusion
Matching each category of matter with its appropriate representative gives: homogeneous mixture corresponds to aqueous glucose solution (p), heterogeneous mixture corresponds to sodium chloride and grain mixture (q), chemical element corresponds to pure copper wire (r), and pure compound corresponds to water ice (s). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(p), B-(q), C-(r), D-(s).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q06 - Solution concentration terms and their defining expressions

questiontext.text:
Match the concentration expressions in List-I with their precise defining characteristics in List-II:

List-I (Concentration Term)List-II (Defining Characteristic)
(A) Molarity(p) Dimensionless ratio of moles of a component to the total moles of all components
(B) Molality(q) Mass of solute present in \(100\text{ g}\) of solution
(C) Mole fraction(r) Number of moles of solute dissolved in \(1\text{ L}\) of solution; temperature-dependent
(D) Mass per cent(s) Number of moles of solute dissolved in \(1\text{ kg}\) of solvent; temperature-independent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate Molarity
Molarity is defined as the number of moles of solute dissolved in one litre of solution: \(M = \frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{V_{\text{solution}}(\text{L})}\). Because volume expands or contracts with changes in temperature, molarity is inherently temperature-dependent.

Step 2: Evaluate Molality
Molality is defined as the number of moles of solute present in one kilogram of solvent: \(m = \frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{w_{\text{solvent}}(\text{kg})}\). Since mass is invariant with temperature, molality is temperature-independent.

Step 3: Evaluate Mole fraction
Mole fraction is defined as the ratio of the number of moles of a particular component to the total number of moles of all constituents present in the mixture: \(\chi_i = \frac{n_i}{\sum n}\). It is a dimensionless quantity.

Step 4: Evaluate Mass per cent
Mass per cent is defined as the mass of solute present per hundred grams of solution: \(\text{Mass \%} = \frac{\text{Mass of solute}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 100\).

Step 5: Final conclusion
Correlating each concentration unit to its precise definition gives: molarity corresponds to (r), molality corresponds to (s), mole fraction corresponds to (p), and mass per cent corresponds to (q). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(r), B-(s), C-(p), D-(q).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q07 - Numerical measurements and their significant figure counts

questiontext.text:
Match the numerical values or counted quantities in List-I with their exact number of significant figures in List-II:

List-I (Measurement / Quantity)List-II (Number of Significant Figures)
(A) \(0.0025\)(p) 5
(B) \(2.005\)(q) 2
(C) \(500.00\)(r) Infinite
(D) \(20\text{ apples}\)(s) 4

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Count significant figures in 0.0025
Zeros preceding the first non-zero digit are leading zeros that serve only to indicate the decimal point and are not significant. In \(0.0025\), the leading zeros are insignificant, leaving only the digits \(2\) and \(5\). Hence, there are \(2\) significant figures.

Step 2: Count significant figures in 2.005
Zeros lying between two non-zero digits are always significant. In \(2.005\), the two zeros between \(2\) and \(5\) are significant. Hence, there are \(4\) significant figures.

Step 3: Count significant figures in 500.00
Trailing zeros in a number that contains a decimal point are significant. In \(500.00\), both the zeros after the decimal point and the zeros between the non-zero digit and the decimal point are significant. Hence, there are \(5\) significant figures.

Step 4: Count significant figures in 20 apples
Counting numbers of distinct discrete objects represent exact numbers with zero uncertainty. Exact numbers can be represented with an infinite number of significant figures by appending decimal zeros (such as \(20.000...\)). Hence, exact counted items possess infinite significant figures.

Step 5: Final conclusion
Matching each quantity with its significant figure count gives: \(0.0025\) corresponds to \(2\) (q), \(2.005\) corresponds to \(4\) (s), \(500.00\) corresponds to \(5\) (p), and \(20\text{ apples}\) corresponds to infinite (r). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(q), B-(s), C-(p), D-(r).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q08 - Substance quantities and total constituent particle counts

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical quantities given in List-I with the total number of constituent atoms or molecules in List-II (Take Avogadro constant \(N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}\), atomic mass of \(\text{He} = 4\text{ u}\), molar mass of \(\text{H}_2\text{O} = 18.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)):

List-I (Sample Quantity)List-II (Total Number of Particles)
(A) \(52\text{ moles of Ar}\)(p) \(13\text{ atoms}\)
(B) \(52\text{ u of He}\)(q) \(1.807 \times 10^{24}\text{ molecules}\)
(C) \(52\text{ g of He}\)(r) \(3.131 \times 10^{25}\text{ atoms}\)
(D) \(54\text{ g of }\text{H}_2\text{O}\)(s) \(7.829 \times 10^{24}\text{ atoms}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Calculate atoms in 52 moles of Ar
Argon is a monoatomic noble gas. One mole of argon contains \(N_A\) atoms: \[ N = n \times N_A = 52\text{ mol} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} = 3.131 \times 10^{25}\text{ atoms} \]

Step 2: Calculate atoms in 52 u of He
A single helium atom has a mass of \(4\text{ u}\). The total number of helium atoms is: \[ N = \frac{\text{Total mass in u}}{\text{Mass of one atom in u}} = \frac{52\text{ u}}{4\text{ u/atom}} = 13\text{ atoms} \]

Step 3: Calculate atoms in 52 g of He
The molar mass of helium is \(4\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). The number of moles is: \[ n = \frac{52\text{ g}}{4\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 13\text{ mol} \] The total number of atoms is: \[ N = 13\text{ mol} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} = 7.8286 \times 10^{24} \approx 7.829 \times 10^{24}\text{ atoms} \]

Step 4: Calculate molecules in 54 g of H2O
The molar mass of water (\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) is \(18.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). The number of moles of water is: \[ n = \frac{54\text{ g}}{18.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 3.0\text{ mol} \] The total number of water molecules is: \[ N = 3.0\text{ mol} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} = 1.8066 \times 10^{24} \approx 1.807 \times 10^{24}\text{ molecules} \]

Step 5: Final conclusion
Matching each sample to its particle count gives: \(52\text{ moles of Ar}\) corresponds to \(3.131 \times 10^{25}\text{ atoms}\) (r), \(52\text{ u of He}\) corresponds to \(13\text{ atoms}\) (p), \(52\text{ g of He}\) corresponds to \(7.829 \times 10^{24}\text{ atoms}\) (s), and \(54\text{ g of }\text{H}_2\text{O}\) corresponds to \(1.807 \times 10^{24}\text{ molecules}\) (q). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(r), B-(p), C-(s), D-(q).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q09 - Stoichiometric chemical processes and quantitative outcomes

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical processes or reaction systems in List-I with their stoichiometric or quantitative outcomes in List-II:

List-I (Process / Reaction System)List-II (Quantitative Outcome)
(A) Complete combustion of \(16.0\text{ g}\) of methane (\(\text{CH}_4\))(p) Produces \(36.0\text{ g}\) of water
(B) Reaction of \(50.0\text{ kg}\) of \(\text{N}_2\) with \(10.0\text{ kg}\) of \(\text{H}_2\) to form ammonia(q) Dihydrogen gas acts as the limiting reagent
(C) Dissolving \(4.0\text{ g}\) of \(\text{NaOH}\) in water to form \(250\text{ mL}\) of solution(r) Yields a solution of molarity \(0.40\text{ M}\)
(D) Thermal decomposition of \(20.0\text{ g}\) of pure \(\text{CaCO}_3\)(s) Produces \(8.80\text{ g}\) of \(\text{CO}_2\) gas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze combustion of methane
The balanced chemical equation is: \[ \text{CH}_4(g) + 2\text{O}_2(g) \to \text{CO}_2(g) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(g) \] Molar mass of \(\text{CH}_4 = 16.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), so \(16.0\text{ g}\) is \(1.0\text{ mol}\). According to stoichiometry, \(1.0\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{CH}_4\) yields \(2.0\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\). With the molar mass of water being \(18.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\), mass of water produced is: \[ 2.0\text{ mol} \times 18.0\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 36.0\text{ g} \]

Step 2: Analyze reaction of N2 and H2
The balanced equation is \(\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \to 2\text{NH}_3(g)\). Number of moles of \(\text{N}_2 = \frac{50.0 \times 10^3\text{ g}}{28.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 1.786 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\). Number of moles of \(\text{H}_2 = \frac{10.0 \times 10^3\text{ g}}{2.016\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 4.960 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\). Stoichiometry requires \(3\) moles of \(\text{H}_2\) per mole of \(\text{N}_2\). For \(1.786 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{N}_2\), the required amount of \(\text{H}_2\) is: \[ 3 \times 1.786 \times 10^3\text{ mol} = 5.358 \times 10^3\text{ mol} \] Since only \(4.960 \times 10^3\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\) is available, dihydrogen gas is completely consumed first and acts as the limiting reagent.

Step 3: Analyze molarity of NaOH solution
Molar mass of \(\text{NaOH} = 23.0 + 16.0 + 1.0 = 40.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). Moles of \(\text{NaOH} = \frac{4.0\text{ g}}{40.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.10\text{ mol}\). Volume of solution in litres is \(250\text{ mL} = 0.250\text{ L}\). Molarity is: \[ M = \frac{0.10\text{ mol}}{0.250\text{ L}} = 0.40\text{ mol L}^{-1} = 0.40\text{ M} \]

Step 4: Analyze decomposition of CaCO3
The decomposition reaction is \(\text{CaCO}_3(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)\). Molar mass of \(\text{CaCO}_3 = 40.0 + 12.0 + 48.0 = 100.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). Moles of \(\text{CaCO}_3 = \frac{20.0\text{ g}}{100.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.20\text{ mol}\). According to stoichiometry, \(0.20\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{CaCO}_3\) produces \(0.20\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{CO}_2\). Molar mass of \(\text{CO}_2 = 44.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). The mass of \(\text{CO}_2\) formed is: \[ 0.20\text{ mol} \times 44.0\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 8.80\text{ g} \]

Step 5: Final conclusion
Matching each process to its outcome shows: combustion of \(16.0\text{ g}\) methane corresponds to producing \(36.0\text{ g}\) water (p), reaction of \(50.0\text{ kg}\) \(\text{N}_2\) with \(10.0\text{ kg}\) \(\text{H}_2\) corresponds to dihydrogen acting as the limiting reagent (q), dissolving \(4.0\text{ g}\) \(\text{NaOH}\) in \(250\text{ mL}\) corresponds to a molarity of \(0.40\text{ M}\) (r), and decomposition of \(20.0\text{ g}\) \(\text{CaCO}_3\) corresponds to forming \(8.80\text{ g}\) \(\text{CO}_2\) (s). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(p), B-(q), C-(r), D-(s).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q10 - Chemical compounds and constituent element mass percentages

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical compounds and designated elements in List-I with their calculated mass percentages in List-II (Take atomic masses: \(\text{H} = 1.008\text{ u}\), \(\text{C} = 12.01\text{ u}\), \(\text{O} = 16.00\text{ u}\), \(\text{Fe} = 55.85\text{ u}\)):

List-I (Compound and Target Element)List-II (Mass Percentage of Element)
(A) Hydrogen in water (\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\))(p) \(52.14\%\)
(B) Carbon in ethanol (\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}\))(q) \(11.18\%\)
(C) Iron in iron(III) oxide (\(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\))(r) \(72.71\%\)
(D) Oxygen in carbon dioxide (\(\text{CO}_2\))(s) \(69.94\%\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Calculate mass percentage of hydrogen in water
Molar mass of \(\text{H}_2\text{O} = 2(1.008) + 16.00 = 18.016\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). Mass of hydrogen in one mole is \(2 \times 1.008 = 2.016\text{ g}\). Mass percentage is: \[ \text{Mass \% H} = \frac{2.016}{18.016} \times 100 = 11.1898\% \approx 11.18\% \]

Step 2: Calculate mass percentage of carbon in ethanol
Molecular formula of ethanol is \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}\) (or \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}\)). Molar mass \(= 2(12.01) + 6(1.008) + 16.00 = 24.02 + 6.048 + 16.00 = 46.068\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). Mass of carbon is \(24.02\text{ g}\). Mass percentage is: \[ \text{Mass \% C} = \frac{24.02}{46.068} \times 100 = 52.140\% \approx 52.14\% \]

Step 3: Calculate mass percentage of iron in iron(III) oxide
Molar mass of \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 = 2(55.85) + 3(16.00) = 111.70 + 48.00 = 159.70\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). Mass of iron is \(111.70\text{ g}\). Mass percentage is: \[ \text{Mass \% Fe} = \frac{111.70}{159.70} \times 100 = 69.9436\% \approx 69.94\% \]

Step 4: Calculate mass percentage of oxygen in carbon dioxide
Molar mass of \(\text{CO}_2 = 12.01 + 2(16.00) = 44.01\text{ g mol}^{-1}\). Mass of oxygen is \(32.00\text{ g}\). Mass percentage is: \[ \text{Mass \% O} = \frac{32.00}{44.01} \times 100 = 72.7107\% \approx 72.71\% \]

Step 5: Final conclusion
Matching each compound with its constituent percentage shows: hydrogen in \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) corresponds to \(11.18\%\) (q), carbon in ethanol corresponds to \(52.14\%\) (p), iron in \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\) corresponds to \(69.94\%\) (s), and oxygen in \(\text{CO}_2\) corresponds to \(72.71\%\) (r). Therefore, the correct matching sequence is A-(q), B-(p), C-(s), D-(r).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Conversion of body temperature to Fahrenheit scale

questiontext.text: Normal human body temperature is \(37.0\ ^\circ\text{C}\). Convert this temperature into degrees Fahrenheit (\(^\circ\text{F}\)). Express your numerical answer rounded to one decimal place.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given temperature in Celsius: \(T = 37.0\ ^\circ\text{C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The relationship between the Fahrenheit and Celsius temperature scales is linear based on standard thermometric fixed points (freezing and boiling points of water).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The interconversion relationship is given by:\[^\circ\text{F} = \frac{9}{5}(^\circ\text{C}) + 32\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(^\circ\text{C} = 37.0\) into the formula:\[^\circ\text{F} = \frac{9}{5}(37.0) + 32 = 9 \times 7.4 + 32 = 66.6 + 32 = 98.6\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated value matches the well-established normal human body temperature of \(98.6\ ^\circ\text{F}\). The final temperature value is 98.6.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Molecular mass calculation of water molecule

questiontext.text: Calculate the molecular mass of water (\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) in unified mass units (\(\text{u}\)) taking the atomic mass of hydrogen as \(1.008\ \text{u}\) and oxygen as \(16.00\ \text{u}\). Express your answer to two decimal places.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Chemical formula of water: \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\).
Atomic mass of \(\text{H} = 1.008\ \text{u}\).
Atomic mass of \(\text{O} = 16.00\ \text{u}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The molecular mass of a covalent compound is the sum of the atomic masses of all the constituent atoms present in one molecule.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Molecular mass of }\text{H}_2\text{O} = 2 \times (\text{atomic mass of H}) + 1 \times (\text{atomic mass of O})\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Molecular mass} = 2 \times (1.008\ \text{u}) + 1 \times (16.00\ \text{u}) = 2.016\ \text{u} + 16.00\ \text{u} = 18.016\ \text{u}\]Rounding to two decimal places gives \(18.02\ \text{u}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The computed value correctly represents the standard molecular mass of water. The final molecular mass value is 18.02.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Moles of carbon atoms in ethane sample

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of moles of carbon atoms present in \(3\ \text{moles}\) of ethane (\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of ethane (\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\)): \(n = 3\ \text{mol}\).
Stoichiometric formula: \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Each individual molecule of ethane contains exactly 2 carbon atoms. Therefore, 1 mole of ethane molecules contains 2 moles of carbon atoms.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Moles of C atoms} = (\text{Moles of }\text{C}_2\text{H}_6) \times 2\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Moles of C atoms} = 3\ \text{mol} \times 2 = 6\ \text{mol}\]The total number of moles of carbon atoms is 6.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio of moles of carbon to moles of ethane is constant and equal to 2. The final value is 6.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Formula mass calculation of sodium chloride

questiontext.text: Calculate the formula mass of sodium chloride (\(\text{NaCl}\)) in unified mass units (\(\text{u}\)), given that the atomic mass of sodium is \(23.0\ \text{u}\) and chlorine is \(35.5\ \text{u}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Chemical substance: Sodium chloride (\(\text{NaCl}\)).
Atomic mass of \(\text{Na} = 23.0\ \text{u}\).
Atomic mass of \(\text{Cl} = 35.5\ \text{u}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Because sodium chloride is an ionic solid consisting of a three-dimensional crystal lattice of \(\text{Na}^+\) and \(\text{Cl}^-\) ions rather than discrete molecules, formula mass is evaluated using its empirical formula unit \(\text{NaCl}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Formula mass of NaCl} = (\text{Atomic mass of Na}) + (\text{Atomic mass of Cl})\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Formula mass} = 23.0\ \text{u} + 35.5\ \text{u} = 58.5\ \text{u}\]The formula mass of sodium chloride is \(58.5\ \text{u}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The sum of the atomic masses yields \(58.5\ \text{u}\), fully consistent with standard chemical literature. The final formula mass is 58.5.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Numerical equality temperature of thermal scales

questiontext.text: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit temperature scales have identical numerical readings? Provide the numerical value (including sign if negative).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Condition of equality: let \(x\) be the temperature at which the numerical reading in Celsius equals that in Fahrenheit, such that \(^\circ\text{F} = ^\circ\text{C} = x\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The thermometric conversion formula is assumed to hold uniformly across negative temperatures.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The conversion equation between Fahrenheit and Celsius scales is:\[^\circ\text{F} = \frac{9}{5}(^\circ\text{C}) + 32\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(^\circ\text{F} = x\) and \(^\circ\text{C} = x\):\[x = \frac{9}{5}x + 32\]Subtract \(\frac{9}{5}x\) from both sides:\[x - \frac{9}{5}x = 32\]\[-\frac{4}{5}x = 32\]Solve for \(x\):\[x = 32 \times \left(-\frac{5}{4}\right) = -40\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Substitute \(-40\) into the formula: \(\frac{9}{5}(-40) + 32 = -72 + 32 = -40\). The reading is identical on both scales. The final value is -40.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Scientific notation addition coefficient evaluation

questiontext.text: Calculate the sum of \(6.65 \times 10^4\) and \(8.95 \times 10^3\) in scientific notation. If the result is written in standard scientific notation as \(N \times 10^4\), find the numerical value of the coefficient \(N\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
First number: \(6.65 \times 10^4\).
Second number: \(8.95 \times 10^3\).
Format requested: \(N \times 10^4\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
To add numbers expressed in scientific notation, they must be converted to have the same power of ten.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Express \(8.95 \times 10^3\) with an exponent of \(4\):\[8.95 \times 10^3 = 0.895 \times 10^4\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Add the two coefficients:\[(6.65 \times 10^4) + (0.895 \times 10^4) = (6.65 + 0.895) \times 10^4 = 7.545 \times 10^4\]Therefore, the coefficient \(N\) is \(7.545\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
In standard scientific notation \(N\) lies between 1 and 10, which \(7.545\) satisfies. The final value of the coefficient is 7.545.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Total number of seconds in two days

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of seconds present in exactly \(2\ \text{days}\) using dimensional analysis.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Time duration: \(2\ \text{days}\).
Target unit: seconds (\(\text{s}\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Standard time unit conversion factors are exact: \(1\ \text{day} = 24\ \text{hours}\), \(1\ \text{hour} = 60\ \text{minutes}\), and \(1\ \text{minute} = 60\ \text{seconds}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Using unit factors:\[\text{Total seconds} = 2\ \text{days} \times \left(\frac{24\ \text{h}}{1\ \text{day}}\right) \times \left(\frac{60\ \text{min}}{1\ \text{h}}\right) \times \left(\frac{60\ \text{s}}{1\ \text{min}}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Total seconds} = 2 \times 24 \times 60 \times 60 = 48 \times 3600 = 172800\ \text{s}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
One day contains \(86400\ \text{seconds}\); two days contain \(2 \times 86400 = 172800\ \text{seconds}\). The final value is 172800.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Distance traversed by light in nanoseconds

questiontext.text: The speed of light in vacuum is \(3.00 \times 10^8\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\). Calculate the distance (in meters) traversed by light in \(2.00\ \text{ns}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of light: \(c = 3.00 \times 10^8\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\).
Time duration: \(t = 2.00\ \text{ns} = 2.00 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Light propagates through vacuum at a constant velocity, following the uniform rectilinear motion relation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Distance } (d) = \text{Speed } (c) \times \text{Time } (t)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[d = (3.00 \times 10^8\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}) \times (2.00 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{s})\]\[d = (3.00 \times 2.00) \times 10^{8 - 9}\ \text{m} = 6.00 \times 10^{-1}\ \text{m} = 0.60\ \text{m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Light travels \(0.3\ \text{m}\) per nanosecond; in \(2\ \text{ns}\) it travels \(0.6\ \text{m}\). The final distance value is 0.6.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Molecular mass calculation of glucose molecule

questiontext.text: Calculate the molecular mass of a glucose molecule (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)) in unified mass units (\(\text{u}\)), using the atomic masses: \(\text{C} = 12.011\ \text{u}\), \(\text{H} = 1.008\ \text{u}\), and \(\text{O} = 16.00\ \text{u}\). Round your final answer to two decimal places.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Formula of glucose: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\).
Atomic masses: \(\text{C} = 12.011\ \text{u}\), \(\text{H} = 1.008\ \text{u}\), \(\text{O} = 16.00\ \text{u}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The molecular mass is obtained by taking the sum of the atomic masses of the individual atoms in the molecular formula.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[M = 6 \times (\text{atomic mass of C}) + 12 \times (\text{atomic mass of H}) + 6 \times (\text{atomic mass of O})\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[M = 6 \times 12.011\ \text{u} + 12 \times 1.008\ \text{u} + 6 \times 16.00\ \text{u}\]\[M = 72.066\ \text{u} + 12.096\ \text{u} + 96.00\ \text{u} = 180.162\ \text{u}\]Rounding to two decimal places yields \(180.16\ \text{u}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated value matches the standard molecular mass of glucose in chemistry textbooks. The final value is 180.16.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Mass percent of carbon in ethanol molecule

questiontext.text: Determine the mass percent of carbon in ethanol (\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}\)). Use molar masses: \(\text{C} = 12.011\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{H} = 1.008\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), and \(\text{O} = 16.00\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\). Express your answer rounded to two decimal places.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molecular formula of ethanol: \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}\).
Molar masses: \(\text{C} = 12.011\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{H} = 1.008\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{O} = 16.00\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Mass percent of an element is the fraction of total molecular mass contributed by that element, multiplied by 100.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Molar mass of }\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} = 2(12.011) + 6(1.008) + 16.00 = 24.022 + 6.048 + 16.00 = 46.07\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\]\[\text{Mass percent of C} = \frac{\text{Mass of C in 1 mol}}{\text{Molar mass of compound}} \times 100\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Mass percent of C} = \frac{24.022\ \text{g}}{46.07\ \text{g}} \times 100 = 52.1424\%\]Rounding to two decimal places gives \(52.14\%\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The sum of percentages of C (\(52.14\%\)), H (\(13.13\%\)), and O (\(34.73\%\)) equals \(100\%\). The final numerical value of mass percent of carbon is 52.14.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Mass percent calculation of solute in solution

questiontext.text: A solution is prepared by dissolving \(2.0\ \text{g}\) of a substance A in \(18.0\ \text{g}\) of water. Calculate the mass percent of the solute A in the solution.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of solute (A): \(m_A = 2.0\ \text{g}\).
Mass of solvent (water): \(m_{\text{solvent}} = 18.0\ \text{g}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Mass is an additive quantity in forming a binary solution: \(\text{Mass of solution} = \text{Mass of solute} + \text{Mass of solvent}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Mass percent of A} = \frac{\text{Mass of A}}{\text{Mass of solution}} \times 100 = \frac{m_A}{m_A + m_{\text{solvent}}} \times 100\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Mass of solution} = 2.0\ \text{g} + 18.0\ \text{g} = 20.0\ \text{g}\]\[\text{Mass percent of A} = \frac{2.0\ \text{g}}{20.0\ \text{g}} \times 100 = 10\%\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio \(2.0 / 20.0 = 0.10\), corresponding exactly to \(10\%\). The final value is 10.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Molarity calculation of sodium hydroxide solution

questiontext.text: Calculate the molarity of an aqueous solution containing \(4.00\ \text{g}\) of \(\text{NaOH}\) in enough water to prepare exactly \(250.0\ \text{mL}\) of solution. (Molar mass of \(\text{NaOH} = 40.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of solute (\(\text{NaOH}\)): \(w = 4.00\ \text{g}\).
Molar mass of \(\text{NaOH}\): \(M_w = 40.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).
Volume of solution: \(V = 250.0\ \text{mL} = 0.250\ \text{L}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The solution is homogeneous and volume is defined by the final prepared volumetric flask level.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Moles of solute } (n) = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Molar mass}} = \frac{w}{M_w}\]\[\text{Molarity } (M) = \frac{n}{V\ (\text{in L})} = \frac{w}{M_w \times V\ (\text{in L})}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[n = \frac{4.00\ \text{g}}{40.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}} = 0.100\ \text{mol}\]\[M = \frac{0.100\ \text{mol}}{0.250\ \text{L}} = 0.400\ \text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1} = 0.400\ \text{M}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
\(0.100\ \text{mol}\) in \(0.250\ \text{L}\) corresponds to \(0.400\ \text{M}\). The final molarity value is 0.4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Volume of stock solution required for dilution

questiontext.text: What volume (in \(\text{mL}\)) of a \(1.50\ \text{M}\) \(\text{HCl}\) stock solution is needed to prepare \(1.00\ \text{L}\) of \(0.300\ \text{M}\) \(\text{HCl}\) solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial concentration: \(M_1 = 1.50\ \text{M}\).
Final concentration: \(M_2 = 0.300\ \text{M}\).
Final volume: \(V_2 = 1.00\ \text{L} = 1000\ \text{mL}\).
Required: Initial volume \(V_1\) in \(\text{mL}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
During dilution, adding pure solvent does not alter the total number of moles of solute present.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The dilution law:\[M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Solve for \(V_1\):\[V_1 = \frac{M_2 V_2}{M_1} = \frac{0.300\ \text{M} \times 1000\ \text{mL}}{1.50\ \text{M}} = \frac{300}{1.50} = 200\ \text{mL}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check moles: \(1.50\ \text{M} \times 0.200\ \text{L} = 0.300\ \text{mol}\); and \(0.300\ \text{M} \times 1.00\ \text{L} = 0.300\ \text{mol}\). Both match exactly. The final volume in milliliters is 200.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Mass of water produced by methane combustion

questiontext.text: Calculate the mass of water (\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) in grams produced by the complete combustion of \(16.0\ \text{g}\) of methane (\(\text{CH}_4\)). (Molar masses: \(\text{C} = 12.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{H} = 1.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{O} = 16.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of methane: \(m = 16.0\ \text{g}\).
Molar mass of \(\text{CH}_4 = 12.0 + 4(1.0) = 16.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).
Molar mass of \(\text{H}_2\text{O} = 2(1.0) + 16.0 = 18.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Combustion is complete in the presence of excess dioxygen.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Balanced chemical equation:\[\text{CH}_4\text{(g)} + 2\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(g)}\]Stoichiometric relation: \(1\ \text{mol}\) of \(\text{CH}_4\) yields \(2\ \text{mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate moles of methane:\[n_{\text{CH}_4} = \frac{16.0\ \text{g}}{16.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}} = 1.00\ \text{mol}\]From stoichiometry, moles of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) produced:\[n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} = 2 \times 1.00\ \text{mol} = 2.00\ \text{mol}\]Mass of water formed:\[\text{Mass} = 2.00\ \text{mol} \times 18.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} = 36.0\ \text{g}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
\(1\ \text{mol}\) \(\text{CH}_4\) (\(16\ \text{g}\)) reacts with \(2\ \text{mol}\) \(\text{O}_2\) (\(64\ \text{g}\)) to give \(1\ \text{mol}\) \(\text{CO}_2\) (\(44\ \text{g}\)) and \(2\ \text{mol}\) \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) (\(36\ \text{g}\)). Conservation of mass: \(16 + 64 = 80 = 44 + 36\). The final mass value in grams is 36.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Atmospheric pressure in pascals from air mass

questiontext.text: The mass of air at sea level is given as \(1034\ \text{g}\cdot\text{cm}^{-2}\). Calculate the atmospheric pressure in Pascals (\(\text{Pa}\) or \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\)). (Take \(g = 9.80\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}\)). Express your answer rounded to the nearest whole number.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of air per unit area: \(\frac{m}{A} = 1034\ \text{g}\cdot\text{cm}^{-2}\).
Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 9.80\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Atmospheric pressure is defined as force per unit area exerted by the column of air above the surface: \(P = \frac{F}{A} = \frac{m \cdot g}{A}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Convert mass and area to SI units:\[1\ \text{g} = 10^{-3}\ \text{kg}\]\[1\ \text{cm}^2 = 10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2\]\[\frac{m}{A} = \frac{1034 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{kg}}{10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2} = 10340\ \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\]\[P = \left(\frac{m}{A}\right) \times g\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[P = 10340\ \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^{-2} \times 9.80\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2} = 101332\ \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^{-2} = 101332\ \text{Pa}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Standard 1 atmosphere is approximately \(101325\ \text{Pa}\). The value \(101332\ \text{Pa}\) closely matches standard atmospheric pressure. The final pressure in pascals is 101332.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Average atomic mass calculation of chlorine isotopes

questiontext.text: Naturally occurring chlorine consists of two isotopes: \(^{35}\text{Cl}\) (molar mass \(34.9689\ \text{u}\)) with natural abundance \(75.77\%\), and \(^{37}\text{Cl}\) (molar mass \(36.9659\ \text{u}\)) with natural abundance \(24.23\%\). Calculate the average atomic mass of chlorine in \(\text{u}\). Round your answer to two decimal places.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Isotope 1: \(^{35}\text{Cl}\), \(m_1 = 34.9689\ \text{u}\), fractional abundance \(f_1 = 0.7577\).
Isotope 2: \(^{37}\text{Cl}\), \(m_2 = 36.9659\ \text{u}\), fractional abundance \(f_2 = 0.2423\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The average atomic mass is the weighted average of the isotopic masses according to their relative fractional natural abundances.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\bar{m} = \sum (f_i \times m_i) = (f_1 \times m_1) + (f_2 \times m_2)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[f_1 \times m_1 = 0.7577 \times 34.9689\ \text{u} = 26.4959\ \text{u}\]\[f_2 \times m_2 = 0.2423 \times 36.9659\ \text{u} = 8.9568\ \text{u}\]\[\bar{m} = 26.4959\ \text{u} + 8.9568\ \text{u} = 35.4527\ \text{u}\]Rounding to two decimal places yields \(35.45\ \text{u}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated value \(35.45\ \text{u}\) is bounded between \(34.97\) and \(36.97\), and is identical to the accepted atomic mass of chlorine in the periodic table. The final average atomic mass is 35.45.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Mass of calcium carbonate reacting with acid

questiontext.text: What mass of \(\text{CaCO}_3\) in grams is required to react completely with \(25.0\ \text{mL}\) of \(0.750\ \text{M}\ \text{HCl}\) according to the reaction:\[\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} + 2\text{HCl}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)}\]Give your answer rounded to two decimal places. (Molar mass of \(\text{CaCO}_3 = 100.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume of hydrochloric acid: \(V = 25.0\ \text{mL} = 0.0250\ \text{L}\).
Molarity of hydrochloric acid: \(M = 0.750\ \text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\).
Molar mass of \(\text{CaCO}_3 = 100.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The reaction proceeds to completion according to the stoichiometric coefficients in the balanced chemical equation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[n_{\text{HCl}} = M \times V\]Stoichiometry: \(2\ \text{moles of HCl}\) react with \(1\ \text{mole of CaCO}_3\):\[n_{\text{CaCO}_3} = \frac{1}{2} n_{\text{HCl}}\]\[\text{Mass of CaCO}_3 = n_{\text{CaCO}_3} \times \text{Molar mass}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[n_{\text{HCl}} = 0.750\ \text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1} \times 0.0250\ \text{L} = 0.01875\ \text{mol}\]\[n_{\text{CaCO}_3} = \frac{0.01875\ \text{mol}}{2} = 0.009375\ \text{mol}\]\[\text{Mass of CaCO}_3 = 0.009375\ \text{mol} \times 100.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} = 0.9375\ \text{g}\]Rounding to two decimal places gives \(0.94\ \text{g}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
\(0.94\ \text{g}\) of \(\text{CaCO}_3\) provides \(\approx 0.0094\ \text{mol}\), which neutralizes \(2 \times 0.0094 = 0.0188\ \text{mol}\) of \(\text{HCl}\). This matches the initial acid content. The final mass in grams is 0.94.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Maximum yield of ammonia from Haber process

questiontext.text: \(50.0\ \text{kg}\) of \(\text{N}_2\text{(g)}\) and \(10.0\ \text{kg}\) of \(\text{H}_2\text{(g)}\) are mixed to produce \(\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}\). Calculate the mass in kilograms of \(\text{NH}_3\) formed. Express your answer to one decimal place. (Molar masses: \(\text{N}_2 = 28.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{H}_2 = 2.016\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{NH}_3 = 17.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of \(\text{N}_2 = 50.0\ \text{kg} = 50.0 \times 10^3\ \text{g}\).
Mass of \(\text{H}_2 = 10.0\ \text{kg} = 10.0 \times 10^3\ \text{g}\).
Molar masses: \(\text{N}_2 = 28.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{H}_2 = 2.016\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), \(\text{NH}_3 = 17.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The reaction goes to completion limited by the reactant that is present in the lower stoichiometric amount (limiting reagent).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Balanced equation:\[\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}\]Stoichiometric ratio of \(\text{N}_2\) to \(\text{H}_2\) is \(1 : 3\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate moles:\[n_{\text{N}_2} = \frac{50.0 \times 10^3\ \text{g}}{28.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}} = 1785.7\ \text{mol}\]\[n_{\text{H}_2} = \frac{10.0 \times 10^3\ \text{g}}{2.016\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}} = 4960.3\ \text{mol}\]To react completely with \(1785.7\ \text{mol}\) of \(\text{N}_2\), required moles of \(\text{H}_2 = 3 \times 1785.7 = 5357.1\ \text{mol}\). However, only \(4960.3\ \text{mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\) are available. Thus, dihydrogen is the limiting reagent.
From stoichiometry, \(3\ \text{mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\) produce \(2\ \text{mol}\) of \(\text{NH}_3\):\[n_{\text{NH}_3} = \frac{2}{3} \times n_{\text{H}_2} = \frac{2}{3} \times 4960.3\ \text{mol} = 3306.9\ \text{mol}\]Mass of \(\text{NH}_3 = 3306.9\ \text{mol} \times 17.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} = 56217\ \text{g} \approx 56.1\ \text{kg}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Total mass formed cannot exceed reactant mass; \(56.1\ \text{kg} < (50.0 + 10.0)\ \text{kg}\). The calculated value correctly reflects the limiting role of dihydrogen. The final mass in kilograms is 56.1.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q19 - Molality calculation of sodium chloride aqueous solution

questiontext.text: The density of a \(3.00\ \text{M}\) solution of \(\text{NaCl}\) is \(1.25\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mL}^{-1}\). Calculate the molality of the solution in \(\text{mol}\cdot\text{kg}^{-1}\). (Molar mass of \(\text{NaCl} = 58.5\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)). Express your answer rounded to two decimal places.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molarity of solution: \(M = 3.00\ \text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\).
Density of solution: \(d = 1.25\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mL}^{-1}\).
Molar mass of solute (\(\text{NaCl}\)): \(M_w = 58.5\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
Consider a basis volume of \(1.00\ \text{L}\) (\(1000\ \text{mL}\)) of solution.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Mass of 1 L solution} = V \times d = 1000\ \text{mL} \times 1.25\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mL}^{-1} = 1250\ \text{g}\]\[\text{Mass of NaCl} = n \times M_w = 3.00\ \text{mol} \times 58.5\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} = 175.5\ \text{g}\]\[\text{Mass of solvent (water)} = \text{Mass of solution} - \text{Mass of solute}\]\[\text{Molality } (m) = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\text{Mass of water} = 1250\ \text{g} - 175.5\ \text{g} = 1074.5\ \text{g} = 1.0745\ \text{kg}\]\[m = \frac{3.00\ \text{mol}}{1.0745\ \text{kg}} = 2.79199\ \text{mol}\cdot\text{kg}^{-1}\]Rounding to two decimal places yields \(2.79\ \text{mol}\cdot\text{kg}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since the solution contains substantial dissolved solute mass, the mass of solvent is slightly greater than \(1\ \text{kg}\), making molality (\(2.79\ \text{m}\)) slightly smaller than molarity (\(3.00\ \text{M}\)), which confirms physical validity. The final molality is 2.79.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOME_BASIC_CONCEPTS_OF_CHEMISTRY_NUMERICAL_Q20 - Molar mass calculation of welding fuel gas

questiontext.text: A welding fuel gas contains only carbon and hydrogen. Burning a small sample of it in oxygen gives \(3.38\ \text{g}\) of carbon dioxide, \(0.690\ \text{g}\) of water and no other products. A volume of \(10.0\ \text{L}\) of this gas measured at STP (where \(1\ \text{mol} = 22.4\ \text{L}\)) is found to weigh \(11.6\ \text{g}\). Calculate the molar mass of the gas in \(\text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\). Express your answer to one decimal place.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume of gas at STP: \(V = 10.0\ \text{L}\).
Mass of gas: \(m = 11.6\ \text{g}\).
Molar volume of ideal gas at standard STP: \(V_m = 22.4\ \text{L}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Model
The fuel gas behaves ideally at standard temperature and pressure according to Avogadro's hypothesis.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Number of moles of gas:\[n = \frac{V}{V_m}\]Molar mass:\[M = \frac{m}{n} = \frac{m \times V_m}{V}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[n = \frac{10.0\ \text{L}}{22.4\ \text{L}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}} = 0.4464\ \text{mol}\]\[M = \frac{11.6\ \text{g}}{0.4464\ \text{mol}} = 25.985\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} \approx 26.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Combustion data confirms the empirical formula is \(\text{CH}\) (formula mass \(13.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)). An empirical formula unit multiplier of 2 gives acetylene (\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\)) with molar mass \(26.0\ \text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\), which is widely utilized as oxy-acetylene welding gas. The final molar mass value is 26.0.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_SOMEBASICCONCEPTSOFCHEMISTRY_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Chronological evolution of foundational atomic and chemical concepts

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following historical milestones in the development of atomic theory and fundamental chemical laws in the correct chronological sequence:

  1. Acharya Kanada formulates the concept of eternal, indivisible building blocks of matter termed Paramānu.
  2. Antoine Lavoisier experimentally establishes the Law of Conservation of Mass during combustion studies.
  3. Joseph Proust formulates the Law of Definite Proportions using natural and synthetic cupric carbonate.
